qs.q: A researcher isolates red blood cells and suspends them in an isotonic solution that is slowly made hypertonic by solute addition. What primary biophysical change occurs in the intracellular fluid?
o: The intracellular macromolecule density falls due to rapid swelling
The internal osmotic pressure drops to match the external level
The internal solute concentration rises as water exits the cell
The cytoplasmic volume increases because of transmembrane currents
The internal potassium level surges to counteract external shifts
qs.e: Water leaves the cell down its concentration gradient, concentrating remaining solutes and raising internal osmolarity.
